title: Task Scheduler
oneLinerQuestion: Calculate minimum CPU units required to finish tasks with compulsory cooldown gaps.
explanation:
Problem Intuition: The Task Scheduler problem requires finding the minimum number of CPU intervals needed to complete a given set of tasks where identical tasks must be separated by at least n cooling intervals. Idle slots must be inserted if no other distinct tasks are ready to run. To minimize idle intervals, we apply a greedy strategy: prioritize the task with the highest remaining frequency, as tasks with greater counts pose the highest risk of forcing downstream idle slots. We implement this using a Max-Heap to always select the most frequent available task, alongside a waiting FIFO Queue to manage cooldown constraints. When a task is executed, its remaining count is decremented; if tasks remain, it is temporarily placed into the queue alongside the timestamp when its cooldown expires (`currentTime + n`). Whenever the front of the queue reaches its unlock timestamp, it is re-enqueued into the Max-Heap.

- Step 1: Frequency Counting & Max-Heap Setup — Count occurrences of each task using a hash map or an array of size 26. Insert all positive frequencies into a Max-Heap (storing counts only, as task identities are interchangeable).

- Step 2: Queue & Clock Initialization — Initialize a queue `waitQueue = []` to store pairs of `[remainingCount, readyTime]` for cooling tasks, and set a global cycle tracker `time = 0`.

- Step 3: Simulation Loop Execution — Execute a while loop that continues as long as either the Max-Heap or the `waitQueue` is non-empty: `while (maxHeap.size() > 0 || waitQueue.length > 0)`.

- Step 4: Advance Clock — Increment the global cycle counter by 1 at each iteration: `time++`.

- Step 5: Greedy Task Dispatch — If the Max-Heap is non-empty, pop the maximum frequency count: `let count = maxHeap.dequeue() - 1`. If `count > 0`, the task still has pending executions, so push it into the cooldown queue with its available time: `waitQueue.push([count, time + n])`. (If the heap is empty, the CPU is forced into an idle slot for this unit of time).

- Step 6: Cooldown Queue Release — Check if any task in `waitQueue` has completed its mandatory cooldown: `if (waitQueue.length > 0 && waitQueue[0][1] === time)`. If ready, pop it from the queue and push its remaining count back into the Max-Heap: `maxHeap.enqueue(waitQueue.shift()[0])`.

- Step 7: Termination & Interval Return — When both the Max-Heap and cooldown queue are completely empty, all tasks have finished executing without violating cooldown rules. Return `time`.

- Complexity & Memory Guarantees — Time Complexity: O(T) where T is the total number of CPU intervals (at most bounded by O(tasks.length * n)), with heap operations taking O(log 26) = O(1) constant time since there are at most 26 distinct uppercase tasks (alternatively solvable in O(tasks.length) using a direct mathematical formula based on max frequency). Space Complexity: O(1) auxiliary space, as the Max-Heap and waiting queue hold at most 26 distinct elements at any point.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION leastInterval(tasks, n):
    count = FREQ_MAP(tasks), maxHeap = MaxHeap(VALUES(count)), q = Queue()
    time = 0
    WHILE maxHeap OR q DO:
        time = time + 1
        IF maxHeap THEN:
            cnt = POP(maxHeap) - 1
            IF cnt != 0 THEN ENQUEUE(q, [cnt, time + n])
        END IF
        IF q AND FIRST(q)[1] == time THEN PUSH(maxHeap, DEQUEUE(q)[0])
    END WHILE
    RETURN time
END FUNCTION
